purpose: Does the skill description fire when it should, and stay quiet when it should not? Twenty realistic requests, ten each way.
how_to_use: Read the description in SKILL.md frontmatter, then judge each query without looking at the expected field. A near-miss that triggers is as much a bug as a hit that does not.

cases.query: Check this MCP server before I install it
проверь этот MCP перед установкой
есть ли тут дырки?
Is this SQL query safe from injection?
Someone reported a CVE in our jsonwebtoken version — is it exploitable for us?
Review this PR before I merge it, it touches the login flow
Our GitHub Actions workflow runs an AI agent with repo secrets. Sanity-check it.
There is an AWS key in the repo history. What now?
Harden this Express app before we go live next week
We are designing a multi-tenant file share. Threat-model it.
This endpoint takes 4 seconds. Make it faster.
Add a login page with email and password fields
cases.why: feature work; no review or audit was requested

cases.query: Rename these variables and split the file, it is getting long
Our tests are flaky on CI. Find out why.
Write the release notes for 3.2
Prettier and eslint disagree about this file. Settle it.
Bump react from 18 to 19 and fix the type errors
cases.why: a version bump for features, not an advisory review

cases.query: The dark-mode toggle does not persist after reload
Explain how this reducer works
Set up a Postgres container for local development
cases.why: local tooling; nothing ships and nothing was asked about hardening

notes: T12 is the hardest near-miss: authentication is mentioned, but the user asked for a feature. Build it following the secure patterns, then offer a review — do not announce an AUDIT.
T17 is the second hardest: a dependency bump becomes SUPPLY-CHAIN only when the user asks about advisories, licences or a compromised package.
